prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right one depends on your budget, what types of plans you want (ACA individual, short‑term, small‑group, HSA‑eligible, association plans), whether you want in‑person help, and whether you need ongoing service (claims help, renewals, tax/1095 support). Instead of naming one definitive firm, here’s a practical way to find the best broker in Kansas City for your situation — plus how I can help.

How to pick the best broker for a self‑employed person
- Look for an independent broker who represents multiple carriers. That ensures more plan options and impartial comparison.  
- Confirm they know ACA (Marketplace) plans and subsidy rules if you might be eligible for premium tax credits.  
- Check experience with sole proprietors and one‑person “small group” arrangements if you want employer‑style coverage.  
- Ask whether they help with HSAs, dental/vision add‑ons, and ACA reporting (Form 1095s).  
- Clarify fees and commissions up front; some brokers are paid only by carriers, some charge client fees for extra services.  
- Prefer someone who provides ongoing service (claims/renewal assistance), not just one‑time enrollment.  
- Read local reviews (Google, Yelp, BBB) and verify licensing with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance.

Where to look
- Search local independent brokers in Kansas City (Google “independent health insurance broker Kansas City MO”) and read reviews.  
- Healthcare.gov “Find Local Help” for certified navigators/CACs — good if you want free unbiased help with Marketplace plans.  
- National brokerages with local offices often operate in KC (HUB International, Alera Group, Brown & Brown, USI, Mercer) if you want a larger firm with broad carrier relationships.  
- National online brokers (eHealth, Stride Health/Truepill-type marketplaces) can be convenient but may not give the same personal service.

Questions to ask a broker before you sign
1. Which carriers and plan types do you offer? (ACA, short‑term, small group, association)  
2. How much do you charge me? How are you compensated?  
3. Do you help with Marketplace subsidy estimates and enrollment?  
4. Will you assist with claims and renewals year‑to‑year?  
5. Do you have experience working with self‑employed/1099 clients in Missouri?  
6. Can you show client references or reviews?

If you want, I can:
- Look up a short list of Kansas City brokers and navigator organizations (I’ll need your ZIP code or preferred neighborhood).  
- Draft the exact questions and a comparison spreadsheet you can use when you talk to 3–4 brokers.  
- Explain subsidy eligibility and whether you should enroll on the Marketplace vs. off‑exchange.

Which of those would you like me to do next? If you share your ZIP code and priorities (price, in‑person service, HSA, dental, etc.), I’ll pull together a tailored shortlist and scripts.
